clue.text: Political representatives setting record in taxes

indicators.note: 'in' says the record piece is placed inside the word for taxes

parts.note: duties are taxes levied on goods
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Politicians are fixing a record level of taxation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' is a link word; the record is set inside the taxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Deputies are elected members of a legislative chamber, as in France's Chamber of Deputies.

clue.text: Corrupt bishop likewise caught in the act

indicators.note: 'caught in' means held inside, so the bishop and likewise go into the act

parts.note: a deed is an act
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
as means likewise, in the same way

explanation.surface: A dishonest bishop is similarly caught red-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught in the act' is an idiom for red-handed, but here 'caught in' is the container signal and 'the act' is DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: To corrupt something is to degrade or lower its quality, which is what debasing means.

clue.text: Communist organization built with poor constituents

indicators.note: 'constituents' asks us to take the parts of 'built' and 'poor' and rebuild them

explanation.surface: A Communist body was formed from impoverished voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' reads as voters, but it signals rearranging the letters BUILT and POOR; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Politburo was the chief policymaking committee of the Soviet Communist Party.

clue.text: Cut large plant and nip in the bud small plant

indicators.note: 'Cut' here means shortened, losing its final letter

parts.note: a tree is a large plant
to foil is to thwart something early

explanation.surface: Someone prunes a big plant and stops a little one from growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' trims TREE to TRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Trefoil is a small clover-like plant with leaves in three parts.

clue.text: Supports goal you expressed with resolution

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

indicators.note: 'expressed' means spoken, so the word 'you' is heard as a single letter

parts.note: the word you, said aloud, sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: Someone backs an aim you stated firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is to bear or tolerate, as one supports a weight or hardship.

clue.text: Half-drunk composer

definitions.meaning: in rhyming slang '... and Liszt' means drunk (pissed), so the composer's name is one half of that slang phrase

explanation.walkthrough: British rhyming slang 'Brahms and Liszt' stands for 'pissed' (drunk); the first half of the phrase is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Brahms wrote four symphonies and the German Requiem, and is half the slang expression for being intoxicated.

clue.text: One means of creating pictures occurred to artist sitting under tree

indicators.note: in a down clue the later pieces sit below the tree

parts.note: the box is a small evergreen tree
came means happened or occurred, as an idea came to him
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An idea came to a painter resting beneath a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A box camera is a simple early camera, a device for taking photographs.

clue.text: Checked books in a university, having dwindled over time

indicators.note: 'over' means spanning, so the dwindled word stretches across the time piece

parts.note: died, as in died away or faded

explanation.surface: Someone inspected the library books at a university that had shrunk over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; 'over' puts DIED round T.
explanation.definitionFit: To audit is to inspect financial accounts, here called books.

clue.text: I'm turning up at golf club to see young woman in play

indicators.note: in a down clue 'turning up' reads the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: taken as the letters I and M
the R and A, the Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews

explanation.surface: Someone arriving at a golf club hopes to watch a girl in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link. The R and A, the Royal and Ancient, is the St Andrews club that governs golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Miranda is the young daughter of Prospero in Shakespeare's The Tempest.

clue.text: Due to madly pursuing boy, it ends with a kiss?

definitions.text: Due to madly pursuing boy, it ends with a kiss?

indicators.note: 'pursuing' puts the anagram after the boy's name

parts.note: Bill is a boy's name

indicators.note: 'madly' says the letters of 'Due to' are scrambled

parts.note: X is the conventional written kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Because of a crazy chase after a boy, it all ends in a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' scrambles the letters of 'Due to'; the X at the end is the kiss, just as a love letter signs off with one.
explanation.definitionFit: A billet-doux is a love letter, which traditionally signs off with a kiss written as a cross.

clue.text: Artist from one of the lower classes

annotationWithheld.why: Artist from one of the lower classes (4): DORE (Gustave Doré) is the artist, but no reading of 'from one of the lower classes' gives the letters; scan and web search give nothing more
annotationWithheld.clue: Artist from one of the lower classes

clue.text: How you desired a goal, and added another red card to the pile

definitions.meaning: to set one's heart on something is to want it badly, so this describes how you longed for an aim

definitions.text: added another red card to the pile
definitions.meaning: read literally, placing one more heart (a red suit) on a stack of cards

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the idiom literally: hearts are a red suit, so laying one on the pile is setting a heart on it.
explanation.definitionFit: To set your heart on something is an idiom for wanting it very much; the card reading is a literal pun.

clue.text: Like Carton and Darnay as match in court

definitions.meaning: Sydney Carton and Charles Darnay in Dickens's A Tale of Two Cities look so alike that one can take the other's place
a tennis match with two players on each side, played on a court

explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link word; 'court' points to tennis, not law, despite the Dickens trial scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Lookalikes are called doubles, and a tennis contest between pairs is a doubles match.

clue.text: Tax collectors cut out most of consumers' options

parts.note: to excise is to cut out

indicators.note: 'most of' says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a menu lists the choices for diners

explanation.surface: Taxmen slashed the bulk of shoppers' choices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims MENU to MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Excisemen were officials who collected excise duty on goods.

clue.text: Notice old man in study being impassive

indicators.note: 'in' tells us the notice and old man go inside the word for study

parts.note: a den is a private study room
AD is short for advertisement, a notice
pa is a colloquial word for father, one's old man

explanation.surface: Someone stays expressionless while reading a notice about an elderly man in the study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link word joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan face or manner shows no emotion, which is exactly what impassive describes.

clue.text: Catering for far-sighted faculty

definitions.meaning: a power of foresight, seeing ahead

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word as PRO (forward) plus VISION (the faculty of sight).
explanation.definitionFit: Provision means supplying necessities such as food, and split as pro-vision it suggests foresight.

clue.text: Launch an enterprise

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to throw or hurl something forward
as a noun, a planned undertaking or scheme

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to hurl forward; as a noun it means a planned undertaking or venture.

clue.text: Jet flier heading north over a city in Italy

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'over' places the earlier pieces above the A

parts.note: a raven is a jet-black bird

indicators.note: 'heading' takes the first letter of north

explanation.surface: A jet plane flies north over an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet' suggests an aeroplane but here means jet black.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravenna is a city in northern Italy famous for its Byzantine mosaics.

clue.text: Person looking after building broken into is in shock

indicators.note: 'is in' says the scrambled letters sit inside the word for shock

parts.note: a jar is a jolt or shock

indicators.note: 'broken' says the letters of into are rearranged

explanation.surface: A caretaker is shocked when the building is burgled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken into' suggests a burglary, but 'broken' alone is the anagram signal and 'is in' puts the result inside the shock.
explanation.definitionFit: A janitor is a caretaker who maintains a building.

clue.text: Observed no subsequent pages, having end removed

parts.note: saw means observed
ff. means 'and following pages' in references

explanation.surface: Someone saw that no further pages came, the document having been cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A sawn-off shotgun has had the end of its barrel cut away, so it is shortened.

clue.text: Heard boy set up device useless at night-time

indicators.note: 'Heard' says a word for boy is said aloud, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: son, a boy, said aloud

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' reads the word for set upwards, backwards

parts.note: laid means set, as a table is laid

explanation.surface: Someone heard a boy put together a gadget that is no good after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundial tells the time by a shadow, so it cannot work without sunlight.

clue.text: It sound like very large part of our capital

indicators.note: 'sound like' says the word for very large is heard, not spelt

parts.note: whopping means enormous

explanation.surface: Something sounds like a huge part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is a link. Wapping is a district of East London by the Thames; 'our capital' is London for a Times reader.
explanation.definitionFit: Wapping is an area of East London, part of the British capital.

clue.text: Tiredness following temperature one had in fever

indicators.note: 'had in' means held inside, so temperature and one go into the fever

parts.note: ague is a fever with shivering fits
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Exhaustion followed a high temperature in a fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatigue is weariness or extreme tiredness.

clue.text: Indication of knife going in? It helps create a sense of perspective

definitions.meaning: read literally, the tip of a blade disappearing as it enters, a playful sense

definitions.text: It helps create a sense of perspective
definitions.meaning: in drawing, the spot on the horizon where parallel lines seem to meet

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: when a knife goes in, its tip disappears from view.
explanation.definitionFit: In perspective drawing, receding parallel lines converge at a single spot on the horizon.

clue.text: Fly back in great anguish from assignation

indicators.note: 'back' says the hidden letters are read in reverse
'in' shows the letters sit inside the words great anguish

explanation.surface: Someone flees in great distress from a secret meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TANG, hidden in 'great anguish', round. 'from assignation' is a second hidden run, the fly sitting forwards in assignation.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a small two-winged fly.

clue.text: Making the most of useful rule, I celebrate

parts.note: a maxim is a rule of conduct or principle
to sing is to celebrate in song

explanation.surface: Someone getting full value from a handy rule throws a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To maximise something is to get the greatest possible value or use from it.

clue.text: A couple of boys joined one of the regular customers

parts.note: Pat is a boy's name
Ron is another boy's name

explanation.surface: Two lads teamed up with a regular at the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joined' is a link word: the two names sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron is a regular client or customer of a shop, restaurant or business.

clue.text: Polish European, for example, invested in weapon

indicators.note: 'invested in' means placed inside, so the example piece goes into the weapon

parts.note: a lance is a long spear used by mounted knights

explanation.surface: A Polish European, say, puts money into arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality, which 'European' seems to support; it is polish meaning refinement.
explanation.definitionFit: Polish in the sense of refinement or sophistication is a synonym of graceful stylishness.
